output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses most likely comes from the 12 August alert relay server move, not from agency nurses. The new server imported only 3 of 14 forwarding rules. The import tool skipped the other 11 and still reported success. The lost rules include a 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 alarms, suppression of repeat notifications, and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone only. Pods A–C then went from about 38 to about 82 phone notifications per nurse per shift, and median acknowledgement time doubled from 34 s to 71 s. Pod D still uses the old server, and its figures didn't change. Incident rates rose equally for core, agency and new-graduate nurses. Bedside alarm volume was flat, so acuity and the 23–24 September monitor update don't explain the rise. Higher sick leave may partly be a result of alarm overload, but the virus season also contributes, so that link is unproven. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis. Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews, which would punish the wrong people. Don't switch off phone forwarding of SpO2 and technical alarms, because nurses rely on the phones. Restore the 11 rules, validate them clinically, and track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Check phone reception in room 14 separately.
